pr_metadata.title: Add a `dump` command in lldb for dumping from ids
pr_metadata.description:
The command is:
```
dump <context> [<ID>|<TYPE><ID>|<TYPE> <ID>|-- <ID>]

TYPE can be "inst", "entity_name", etc.
```

This saves a lot of typing of `SemIR::MakeInstId()` in a debugger, and allows copy-pasting ids from dump output, as they take the form `inst33`, etc.

gold_comments._reviewer_comment_full:
Just looking one more time at the code structure, had you considered putting the final print in a helper function, like `def print_id`, similar to `print_usage`? Mainly I was wondering because of the `if not id_type` flow, which I assume you're doing so that the `print_usage` calls return to where you want. But then I was thinking about nesting, and not sure what you'd think of something like:

```
    print_id(f"SemIR::...")
    return
```

which by the return, would mean you wouldn't need as much nesting.

Anyways, I think this code is plenty good as-is, so I'm going to approve and leave this to you to choose.
